props.statement: The amounts of mixed adsorption at 250 °C were greater than those at 300 °C.

props.name: adsorbed H2 to CO ratio nearly 1.5, as observed earlier during reaction
props.statement: When both gases fall on curves (h) and (c), the ratio of adsorbed hydrogen to carbon monoxide is nearly 1.5, agreeing with that observed during the reaction in the earlier paper.

props.name: about 85% of the catalyst surface is covered by the adsorbed species (cross-section 25 Å2)
props.statement: About 85% of the catalyst surface is covered by the adsorbed species during the experiments, taking a cross-sectional area of 25 Å2 for the species (presumably CH3O); in some cases the sum of adsorbed H2 and CO exceeded the BET v_m of 1.52 ml, which does not contradict complex formation.

props.name: adsorption during methanol decomposition exceeds equilibria; after decomposition it matches mixed adsorption
props.statement: Hydrogen and carbon monoxide adsorbed during methanol decomposition exceed their separate adsorption equilibria, and the adsorption after the decomposition agrees with the mixed adsorption curves.

props.name: earlier proposed mechanisms (cited): termolecular (Natta et al.), bimolecular via formaldehyde, methanol desorption, Knudsen diffusion
props.statement: Mechanisms proposed earlier include a termolecular surface reaction of two adsorbed hydrogen molecules and adsorbed CO (Natta, Mazzanti and Pasquon), a bimolecular scheme via formaldehyde with either step rate-determining (Natta and Pastonesi; Ozaki and Saita; Pasquon), rate-determining desorption of methanol (Uchida and Ogino), and Knudsen diffusion of methanol in the pores (Cherednichenko and Temkin).

props.name: rate and equilibrium amounts of H2 and CO chemisorption are mutually enhanced by the other gas
props.statement: The rate as well as the equilibrium amounts of chemisorption of hydrogen and of carbon monoxide on the three-component methanol synthesis catalyst are mutually enhanced by the presence of the other gas; mixed adsorption exceeds separate adsorption.

props.name: earlier paper (cited): r = k P_H2 A_CO; adsorbed species CH3O not CH2O; Eley-Rideal reaction of H2 gas with adsorbed CH3O rate-determining

evidence.note: rendered: 'is CH3O and not CH2O'; quote withheld: sha256:2a6eb73f119c17d07c254cac8beae04caef47ce7c3d7950454d8c759c6a1c167 chars:80

props.note: cited from Tsuchiya and Shiba, Shokubai 4, 27 (1962); not this paper's measurement
props.statement: In the authors' earlier paper (ref. 10), by Tamaru's method, the methanol synthesis rate was r = k P_H2 A_CO (A_CO: CO adsorbed in any surface complex), or Uchida-Ogino's equation with α nearly 0.7; the adsorbed species had the stoichiometric formula CH3O, not CH2O; the reaction between hydrogen gas and adsorbed CH3O (Eley-Rideal type) was concluded to be rate-determining.

props.name: the mutual enhancement of adsorption has a certain saturation
props.statement: The mutual enhancement of adsorption has a certain saturation (knick points in Fig. 4), suggesting some excess adsorption of either gas that does not form a complex, though small.

props.name: alternatively: creation of additional sites (Zn-H) by H2 chemisorption (Nagarjunan, Sastri and Kuriacose)
props.statement: The enhancement might be due to the creation of additional sites: hydrogen chemisorption creates additional donor levels, reduces the surface charge barrier and forms e.g. Zn-H bonds favourable for CO adsorption, while CO facilitates Zn-H formation.

props.name: mutual enhancement explained by surface-complex formation
props.statement: The mutual enhancement of H2 and CO adsorption is explained by the formation of a surface complex; on this typical three-component catalyst and at these temperatures complex formation is highly probable.

props.name: the surface complex (at least its major part) is the intermediate of methanol synthesis
props.statement: The surface complex formed is the intermediate of the methanol synthesis reaction; at least a major part of the adsorbed species is the reaction intermediate.

props.name: curves after decomposition represent equilibria between H2, CO and methanol
props.statement: Since adsorption after methanol decomposition agrees with mixed adsorption and only very little methanol (less than 0.2%) is in the gas at equilibrium, these curves conceivably represent equilibrium states between hydrogen, carbon monoxide and methanol.

props.name: rate-determining step: molecular hydrogen reacting with the surface complex
props.statement: The rate-determining step of the overall methanol synthesis is the reaction between hydrogen gas (molecules) and the adsorbed surface complex, since the exponent of P_H2 in Eq. (1) is unity (it would be 0.5 if hydrogen atoms reacted).

props.name: the covering species is presumably CH3O
props.statement: The adsorbed species covering about 85% of the surface is presumably CH3O.
